text.p: Shares in Fortis AG, the Belgian arm of Belgo-Dutch financial group Fortis, lost more than 1.5 percent as investors saw news of the subscription price for its capital increase as an opportunity to take profits.

"It is normal when you have a capital increase that there is selling pressure and we had not seen this until now when the price was set," analyst and trader Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen said on Wednesday.
By 1210 GMT the share was down 1.54 percent at 5,770 francs.
"The price has come down because of the dilution of one new share for 12 existing ones," said another trader.
"There is also some weakness in Fortis resulting from some arbitrage," he added.

Dealers said recent talk that Fortis had decided not to bid for Scottish Amicable, which Fortis declined to comment on, was not a reason for the share price fall. Instead, the market would welcomed such a move.
Fortis on Tuesday set the subscription price for its 17 billion Belgian francs capital increase at 5,040 francs per share.
